_why: The plugin's unit tests must be able to fail the way reality fails. Every bug found so far was found by reading rows like these, not by a synthetic case: (1) `arguments` is a JSON string in the real session log, not an object; (2) `repo.available` was missing from the facts, making an unreadable repository indistinguishable from a clean one; (3) `[exit code: N]` carries the shell host's code, not the child's.

This row is only reachable when the `arguments` JSON-string fix is in place: before it, every command parsed as empty and tests_run was permanently false.

_exit_code_measurement._why: The marker contract was measured directly, because assuming it would have been wrong in a way that only shows up as 'slightly suspicious numbers' in a log nobody re-reads.
_exit_code_measurement._authoritative_source: @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-pwsh/lib/index.js:59-79 `renderPwshResult` builds the model-facing text as `body` followed by markers, pushing `[exit code: ${result.exitCode}]` ONLY when `result.exitCode !== 0` and only as the LAST line. `result.exitCode` is the pwsh HOST process's code (dsh-pwsh-local/lib/index.js:364-368 assigns `proc.exitCode = outcome.exitCode`). The marker is therefore absent on success and carries the host code on failure.

observations.note: pwsh normalises a non-zero child status to 1 at the host level. Measured in this session, twice, by two independent runs.
Coincides, which is exactly why the 7 case had to be measured.
renderPwshResult adds no marker for exit 0 — so 'no marker' means success, and parseExitCode's 0 default is the contract, not a guess.

_exit_code_measurement.conclusion: The marker is authoritative for ZERO versus NON-ZERO and must not be read as a child process's exact exit status. This matches DSH's own contract: `parseExitStatus` in @deepseek-ai/dsh-shell (lib/index.js:31-46) recovers `exitCode` from this marker and nothing else.

_truncation_measurement._why: The same real output that carries the exit marker is also the output most likely to be long. Whether the reader keeps the head or the tail decides whether a failing test suite is reported as failing.

_consequences_before_fix: Budget reset: every `subagent-settled` and every `plugin (hindsight)` injection started a new 'user task', so `assessmentsUsed` was zeroed several times per real task. The 3-per-task ceiling silently stopped existing, and because a reset is not an error and writes no row, the log looked healthy throughout.

Fabricated goal: `goal` takes the FIRST non-excluded user-role message. In this session the second one is an `agent-instructions` block, so on any turn where the human's message was not first, Jev would be asked whether a SYSTEM REMINDER had been completed.
_user_message_source_measurement._fix: An allow-list: `isUserAuthored(source)` returns `source?.kind === 'user'` (lib/taskstate.js), used by both `deriveEvents`' goal extraction and the outcome-backfill task boundary in lib/index.js. A future synthetic source then defaults to 'not the human', failing toward assessing less rather than toward an unbounded budget.
_user_message_source_measurement._dsh_contract: DSH's own MessageSourceMap (@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets/lib/typert.host.js:613) lists: user, plugin, model, tool, 'user-rpc' (which maps to kind 'user'), 'agent-message', 'subagent-settled', 'skill-invocation', 'team-message', goal, 'session-reference'. Note that the map is a TYPE declaration; the runtime kinds actually observed are the ones counted above, including several (agent-instructions, skill-catalog) that the declaration does not name at all — which is itself the reason an allow-list is the safe shape.

_exit_attribution_measurement._why: The SECOND fabricated-pass bug, and subtler than truncation: DSH's `[exit code: N]` marker carries the SHELL HOST's exit code, which in Windows PowerShell belongs to the LAST STATEMENT. An agent that wraps a call to capture its output therefore hides the real result. On the first real-Jev round a subagent wrote that wrapper, and a suite that really failed (npm exit 1) was recorded as `tests_passed: true` — the plugin's own evidence was wrong while the agent's claim was honest.
_exit_attribution_measurement._measured_by: tools/measure-exit-shapes.mjs — each shape is RUN for real in a child shell, and the observed exit code is compared against the true outcome.
_exit_attribution_measurement._shell: C:\WINDOWS\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe — PowerShell 7 is NOT installed on this machine, and `dsh-pwsh-local`'s resolver falls back to 5.1, so 5.1's behaviour is the contract that matters.

_exit_attribution_measurement._rule_derived: With ONE statement the marker is the command's own code. With SEVERAL, the code belongs to the last one, unless that last statement is an explicit `exit $LASTEXITCODE` passthrough. `exitCodeIsAttributable(command, kind)` implements exactly this and matches every measured shape.
_exit_attribution_measurement._verdict_rule: A command whose code cannot be attributed is recorded with `exit_attributable: false` and votes for NEITHER outcome, so `tests_passed` becomes null (unknown). Recording it as true was the bug; recording it as false would fabricate an accusation. `lib/taskstate.js` derives the tri-state, and `lib/log.js` writes `facts.unattributable_exits_n` so the rate is measurable offline.
_exit_attribution_measurement._verified_against_real_commands: tools/replay-real-commands.mjs replays the verbatim commands from sessions 3d99a91c and ebc5ed01: the wrapped commands now yield UNKNOWN, the unwrapped one still yields FAILED, and no failed run is misread as a verdict.
